transcript: Last night, I saw a new play called N/A at Lincoln Center. This is a two hander about a couple of congresswomen who are unnamed but who are obviously Nancy Pelosi and AOC. This 80 minute one act gives a portrait of the ideological clashes between what performative progress and true progress look like. Despite the fact that the acting is pretty convincing in the portrayals of these well known political figures, I think it's best to try to see this piece as historical fiction cause I don't really imagine Nancy Pelosi and AOC ever really having these kinds of conversations as directly as they do in this play. I thought this play was more interesting as a concept than in practice, it's not really a plot driven thing, so while the conversations progressed well, the overall experience felt a little underseasoned. In fairness I also think I'm feeling a bit burnt out from “political” theater. I think if you enjoy these kinds of debates for what they are, and you don't really mind a somewhat surface level dramatization of them, you'll enjoy this. Otherwise, I wouldn't say it's a must see. With that, another program for my collection.
